title: Masala Dosa
description: Paper-thin fermented rice and lentil crêpes, crisp at the edges, folded around a turmeric potato filling. The South Indian breakfast.
notes: The batter keeps four days in the fridge and gets pleasantly sourer. Serve with coconut chutney and sambar.

steps.text: Rinse the idli rice, and separately the urad dal with the fenugreek seeds, then soak each in plenty of water.
Grind the dal to a light, fluffy paste and the rice slightly coarser, using as little water as possible. Mix together with the salt.
steps.tip: The dal should look like whipped cream. That air is what the fermentation builds on.

steps.text: Cover and ferment in a warm place overnight, until risen and sour-smelling.
steps.tip: Below about 25°C it can take a full day. An oven with only its light on is warm enough.

steps.text: Fry the mustard seeds in the neutral oil until they pop, then add the curry leaves, onion, green chillies, and ginger and cook until soft.
Add the turmeric and salt, then the potatoes, roughly crushed, and a splash of water. Stir until it holds together loosely.

Thin the batter with water to a pouring consistency. Heat a flat griddle, wipe it with a little ghee, and ladle batter into the centre, spreading it in a fast outward spiral with the back of the ladle.
steps.tip: If the batter sticks and will not spread, the griddle is too hot — sprinkle it with water and wipe.

steps.text: Drizzle ghee around the edge and cook until the underside is golden and crisp and the edges lift.
Spoon potato masala down the middle, fold, and serve at once.
